samples.summary: Non-ASCII characters in a URL path truncate the span, so the link navigates to a wrong (truncated) destination instead of not linking
samples.evidence: `URL_CHAR` (line 36) contains only RFC 3986 ASCII characters. A pasted URL with a non-ASCII path — common in exactly the Korean Confluence/Notion sheets the fixtures in `cell-links.test.ts` are drawn from, e.g. `https://wiki.example.com/x/기획문서` — stops the forward walk at the first Hangul byte. `detectLinks` then emits a span of `https://wiki.example.com/x/`, which parses and passes `isSafeUrl`, so a *truncated* URL is painted, recorded as a hit box and handed to `window.open`. The same file argues the opposite policy for the length bound (line 293: "linking a truncated destination is worse than linking nothing"), and that reasoning is not applied here. No test covers a non-ASCII path.

samples.summary: The "keep the card open across the gap between two links" fallback never fires for merged cells or overflowing text — the two cases its own comment says it exists for
samples.evidence: `updateLinkHover` falls back to `toSref(this.toRefFromMouse(x, y))` and asks `linksInCell(candidate)`. But the painter records `sref = toSref(id)` for the *anchor* cell (gridcanvas.ts:1775), while `toRefFromMouse` resolves a merged cell's covered sub-cell and an overflowed line's neighbouring cell. So for precisely the wide cells the comment at line 961-966 names, hovering the plain text between two spans yields `candidate` != the painted sref, `linksInCell` returns `[]`, `sref` becomes null and the card is closed and re-opened (300 ms strobe) while crossing one cell.

samples.summary: `navigator.clipboard` is undefined on an insecure origin, so the copy button throws a synchronous TypeError instead of taking the documented rejection path
samples.evidence: `navigator.clipboard.writeText(url).then(...)` — the `.then(onRejected)` handler only covers a *rejected promise*. The comment immediately above lists "an insecure origin" as a case it handles, but on an http:// origin (self-hosted deployments) `navigator.clipboard` is `undefined` and the property access throws a TypeError out of the React onClick handler, uncaught. The test only stubs a rejecting `writeText`, never an absent `clipboard`.

samples.summary: `e.detail === 1` also swallows a legitimate second click made within the double-click interval
samples.evidence: The guard is on `handleMouseDown`, where `detail` counts *any* rapid successive presses, not only presses on the same target. A read-only viewer clicking two different links in a list within ~500 ms, or clicking the same link twice to open two tabs, gets `detail === 2` on the second press and nothing opens. A per-link or timestamp-based guard would express the intent ("do not fire twice for one double-click") without rejecting the second real click.

samples.summary: Splitting a line into per-span `fillText` calls breaks shaping/kerning across the span boundaries and mis-orders bidirectional text
samples.evidence: The span branch draws `line.slice(cursor, span.start)`, `line.slice(span.start, span.end)`, ... as independent `fillText` calls positioned by `measure()` of the preceding prefix. Canvas shapes each call independently, so kerning pairs and combining marks that straddle a span edge render differently from the `spans.length === 0` path, and for an RTL/bidi line the per-segment layout no longer matches the logical-to-visual reordering a single `fillText` would perform — the text is drawn in the wrong visual order, and the recorded hit boxes follow it.

samples.summary: `toLabel` drops the fragment, so two links differing only by `#anchor` render identical labels
samples.evidence: `const tail = `${parsed.pathname}${parsed.search}`` omits `parsed.hash`. A cell holding `…/doc#section-a` and `…/doc#section-b` shows the same label twice, which defeats the card's stated purpose of making the destination legible (the full URL is only in `title`).

samples.summary: When every URL is filtered out the wrapper stays mounted at the previous cell's coordinates
samples.evidence: `SheetLinkPopover` returns `null` when `safe.length === 0`, so `wrapper.getBoundingClientRect()` is 0×0 and the layout effect returns early at line 1643 without clearing `linkPopoverPos`. The wrapper then renders `visibility: visible` at the *previous* cell's left/top. Harmless today (the div is empty) but it is a stale-state path that any future non-empty fallback content would surface.

finding.summary: Non-ASCII characters in a URL path truncate the span, so the link navigates to a wrong (truncated) destination instead of not linking
finding.evidence: `URL_CHAR` (line 36) contains only RFC 3986 ASCII characters. A pasted URL with a non-ASCII path — common in exactly the Korean Confluence/Notion sheets the fixtures in `cell-links.test.ts` are drawn from, e.g. `https://wiki.example.com/x/기획문서` — stops the forward walk at the first Hangul byte. `detectLinks` then emits a span of `https://wiki.example.com/x/`, which parses and passes `isSafeUrl`, so a *truncated* URL is painted, recorded as a hit box and handed to `window.open`. The same file argues the opposite policy for the length bound (line 293: "linking a truncated destination is worse than linking nothing"), and that reasoning is not applied here. No test covers a non-ASCII path.

verdict.reason: The claimed code is present and behaves as described. `URL_CHAR` (cell-links.ts:36) is ASCII-only, so the forward walk at line 292 stops at the first non-ASCII path character. The `overlong` guard (lines 296-297) only triggers when `end === limit` (the MaxUrlLength bound), so a walk halted by a non-URL character keeps the truncated prefix at line 298. `trimTrailing` does not strip `/` (line 102), `shaped` passes for a non-`www.` scheme (lines 302-304), and `toUrl`/`isSafeUrl` (core/src/url/index.ts:58-65) accept `https://wiki.example.com/x/`, so a span for the truncated URL is emitted at line 307. It is then painted and laid out as a hit box (gridcanvas.ts:1696, 1800) and passed unmodified to `window.open` (worksheet.ts:3704). No guard elsewhere normalizes or rejects it. The file's own stated policy at lines 293-295 ("linking a truncated destination is worse than linking nothing") is not applied here, and the Korean-language fixtures in the test file (lines 34, 42-44, 89) all use ASCII paths, so no test covers this. Wrong navigation destination on a realistically reachable path = major correctness bug.
